openPoints: RESOLVED — CRITICAL #1 (transport reachability). Verified on disk: transport.ts:242-251 dispatches into tools/eap.ts, which now calls eapServices() at lines 314, 507 and 618; services.ts wires SqlitePromotionRepository/ContestationRepository/RecallRepository/ApprovalRepository/AuditRepository into PromotionService, ContestationService, RecallWorker and CapabilityGateway; index.ts:419 exposes eap(tenantId) so the gateway and admitPersistentDelta have a production entry point. eapPromote now requires a candidate row in state 'verified' in the child horizon (eap.ts:348-371) and eapContest runs validateEvidence plus unresolvedTargets against the caller's own tenant (eap.ts:494, 448-454). There is one implementation. No further deduction.

RESOLVED — CRITICAL #2 (fake recall). Verified: the `recalls` table is gone (db.ts:176-179 records the removal), SqliteDependencyQuery.reverseClosure (dependency-query.ts:37-63) computes a real transitive reverse closure from the claims.refs edges, and eapRecall drives RecallWorker.processBatch over recall_cases/recall_checkpoints/recall_scars with durable checkpoints and a scar. RecallProgressed and TruthOwnershipSuspended are now appended (eap.ts:681, 693), closing half of the prior MEDIUM event finding. No further deduction.

TIER 1 — The recall closure is computed and checkpointed, but the degradation is applied only to the throwaway Maps that buildRecallExecutionContext (dependency-query.ts:72-102) rebuilds per call: stepRecall mutates ctx.claimStates and ctx.cellOwners (graph-core/src/eap/recall.ts:206, 217) and nothing writes those back to `claims`, `candidates` or `authority`. The stated justification — that the authority column has no 'suspended' value and this is therefore an ADR-level decision — is contradicted by watch-bridge.ts:101, which already persists `value: "suspended"` into that exact table through the same write() path, and by 003 §Events line 207, which names the authority view a consumer of TruthOwnershipSuspended (003 defers only the destination status of INDIRECT dependents, not whether suspension is projected at all). If graph.query, graph.impact and authority.flip keep reading a recalled claim as admitted and a suspended cell as graph-owned after cognitive.recall returns status 'completed', which reader of this graph ever learns that the premise was retracted?

TIER 2 — validateOperatorApproval (graph-core/src/eap/capabilities.ts:143) still compares the stored basedOnSeq against currentSeq, and authorizeCapability (line 178) sources that value from request.currentSeq — the caller's own field. Expiry now fails closed on a non-instant (capabilities.ts:128-141) and the stored grant supplies scope and the consumed flag, so the only remaining freedom is the one that matters: the requester asserts its own freshness. If a client can pick the sequence its approval is checked against, what stops an operator grant issued for one state of the horizon from being spent against a later, materially different one?

TIER 2 — eapRecall is now async and its idempotency guard is not transactional: `await services.recallRepo.get(recallId)` (eap.ts:634) yields, and only afterwards does the caller allocate a sequence (line 662) and `await services.recalls.initiateRecall` (line 665), whose repo.create writes upsert-style through write(). Two concurrent cognitive.recall calls on the same contestationId interleave at those await points inside a SINGLE Bun process — this is not the cross-process case that was scoped out — so both observe no existing case, both burn a `recalls` sequence and both drive processBatch over the same closure. What makes 'idempotent by contestation' true when the read that establishes it and the write that satisfies it are separated by two microtask boundaries and no BEGIN IMMEDIATE?

TIER 2 — Whole-tenant materialization remains on every hot path. incrementalGate (gates.ts:166) still spreads the entire roundtrip index per invocation and admitPersistentDelta calls it once per candidate (persistent-delta.ts:138), so the per-batch buildRoundtripIndex fix removed the re-parse but left the O(candidates x claims) copy; persistent-delta.ts:118-119 structuredClones state.graphs and state.claimsCache on every admission; and one recall performs three synchronous full-table scans (dependency-query.ts:38, 77, 89) plus a full JSON re-serialization of the case state per batch through write() to both SQLite and the JSONL mirror (eap-repositories.ts:252-266), which is quadratic in the closure when a caller passes a small batchSize. For a 100k-claim tenant, what is the event loop doing for the duration of an admission burst, and what does the mirror file look like after a 10k-claim closure processed one at a time?

TIER 3 — Carried forward, disclosed and unfixed, deducted once as a cluster: eapInitiate is still the one adapter that never enters serialTransaction (eap.ts:102) while HorizonStore.create does read-then-upsert; persistent-delta.ts:174-178 still takes COALESCE(MAX(seq),0) for cs_deltas inside a DEFERRED unit; PromotionService.getEvents (eap-repositories.ts:126), getProposalsForParent and the audit list() materialize whole tenant tables with no pagination and promotion_events has no retention policy; and the unguarded JSON.parse calls (eap-repositories.ts:130, 139, 186, 187, 342, 348, 365) throw a raw SyntaxError out of the tool boundary instead of a typed Refusal on any column a rebuildFromJsonl replay left malformed — note that dependency-query.ts:21-29 already models the guarded form. Why does the one new file parse defensively while the repository it feeds does not?

TIER 3 — MAX_RECALL_BATCHES (eap.ts:584) caps the drive loop at 10,000 iterations, after which eapRecall returns ok:true with whatever status settled holds — 'active' for an unfinished case — carrying a checkpoint but no refusal, no resumption token and no distinct signal in the response envelope. 003 lists large-closure batching limits among the deferred ADR boundaries, so silently exiting the loop decides that boundary rather than stopping at it. How does a client distinguish 'this recall finished' from 'this recall ran out of batches' in the payload it actually receives?
architectureTip: The governed aggregates are now the only writer, but recall still stops at the write model: give the Recall Case a projection step that applies its durable degradation and suspension to the read model (claims, candidates, authority) inside the same unit that checkpoints it, so a completed recall and a queryable graph cannot disagree about what is still admitted.
